chapter: Dancing schools and Charlie Johnson in New York
title: Ben Whitted, lead alto with Charlie Johnson
summary: McRae remembers the Hampton-schooled altoist Ben Whitted as a gentleman, pipe-smoking and clean living, who walked home with him and Benny Waters.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Ben Witted, that was the alto player I told you that Ben Waters and I stayed with. Great alto. Great musician.
Where was he from and what was some of his outstanding qualities? I've heard of him before.
Well, I never -- I think Ben Witted was from Hampton.

I think he went to school there. Ben Witted was an outstanding -- in the first place, he was just an outstanding gentleman. His quality of a man was so beautiful to be around that it remind you of, you know, like a

school teacher or something. You know, a guy that's a doctor or something like that, those fellows (inaudible).
Clean living, you know. He smoked a pipe -- always liked that pipe. We used to walk home together and it be cold, he would light that pipe up.
And we'd walk -- I'd say, "Come on, Ben, take a cab." He say, "No, we only live up 140th Street." We walked to 140th Street -- to 135th. Walked the hill, you know.
And it would be cold. And he'd just walk us up there, and Ben Waters and I, we'd be following him. We stayed with him for quite a while.
He was a great musician. I think he learned his music in school. I think he came out of the school band.
I'm quite sure he was a great clarinet player -- great alto. He was a lead alto player for Charlie Johnson for years.
Then there, of course, Bennie Waters --
